rules.description: The applicant's household must appear in the SECC 2011 (or subsumed RSBY) PM-JAY beneficiary database, identified via rural deprivation criteria or urban occupational category.
rules.user_friendly_explanation: PM-JAY is not something you apply for from scratch - the government already has a list of eligible families based on a 2011 household survey. You need to check if your family is on that list.
rules.pass_message: Your household appears to match PM-JAY's SECC 2011 inclusion pattern based on the details you gave - but this MUST be confirmed on the official portal before relying on it.
rules.fail_message: Based on what you've told us, your household does not match the known SECC 2011 inclusion patterns for PM-JAY. You may still want to check directly, since state-specific extensions can add more families.
rules.unknown_message: We can't tell if your family is in the SECC 2011 database from the information given. Please check directly at beneficiary.nha.gov.in using your mobile number, Aadhaar, or ration card.

rules.description: For urban households, membership in one of the 11 officially listed occupational categories is one recognised path to SECC 2011-based inclusion.
rules.user_friendly_explanation: If you live in a city/town and your main earner works in one of a specific list of jobs (like street vendor, domestic worker, rickshaw puller, construction labourer, etc.), that's one of the ways a family gets included.
rules.pass_message: Your stated occupation matches one of the 11 urban categories PM-JAY uses for inclusion. This increases the likelihood of eligibility but does not confirm it - the household still needs to appear in the official database.
rules.fail_message: Your stated occupation does not match PM-JAY's urban inclusion list. You may still be eligible via the rural deprivation criteria or a state-specific extension.
rules.unknown_message: Occupation was not provided, so this pre-screening check could not be run.

rules.description: For rural households, meeting at least one SECC 2011 deprivation criterion (D1-D5, D7) or an automatic-inclusion category is one recognised path to inclusion.
rules.user_friendly_explanation: If you live in a village and your household matches certain hardship markers from the 2011 census (like having only one room with a mud roof, no working-age adult, a disabled member with no able-bodied adult, being SC/ST, or being a landless labourer family), that's one of the ways a family gets included.
rules.pass_message: Your household matches at least one SECC 2011 rural deprivation/inclusion criterion. This increases the likelihood of eligibility but does not confirm it - the household still needs to appear in the official database.
rules.fail_message: Your household does not appear to match the rural deprivation/inclusion criteria based on what you've told us.
rules.unknown_message: Not enough information was provided to check rural deprivation criteria.

rules.description: There is no restriction on family size for benefit eligibility once a household is included - the Rs 5 lakh cover is a family floater with no member limit (unlike the old RSBY, which capped at 5 members).
rules.user_friendly_explanation: However many people are in your family, they can all share the same yearly cover - there's no cut-off number of family members.
rules.pass_message: Not applicable as a gating condition - informational only.
rules.fail_message: Not applicable - this condition cannot fail.
